gen-righteous-gf-alumni-sans-sc: Righteous bends what feels like thin steel rod into fat-bowled letters, every curve holding its width without a wobble. Alumni Sans SC tucks in beneath, tightly spaced, with a faint thick-thin shift.
gen-righteous-gf-anaheim: Righteous looks cut from bent wire, its big bowls pressing right up against the edges of the line. Shrink it down, though, and Anaheim's rounded, dense text would simply take over.
gen-righteous-gf-arsenal: Righteous draws every letter without a single hairline, just rod-like strokes and bowls that crowd the line. It handles the shouting; Arsenal, with its gentle stroke shifts, handles the talking.
gen-righteous-gf-arsenal-sc: Arsenal SC keeps things quiet, tight and softly shaded. Righteous, with strokes like bent plastic tubing, then jumps in over it, and the gap between loud and hushed does the work.
gen-righteous-gf-basic: Loud, round, a little playful: Righteous fills its line with bowls and an s whose spine is as thick as its ends. Basic follows in sans-serif, modest and tidy, barely lifting its capitals.
gen-righteous-gf-cal-sans: Cal Sans runs one stroke width through the whole alphabet, with short ascenders and a tall x-height. Righteous is the one for bold, bent-rod attention-grabbing, while Cal Sans simply carries the sentences.
gen-righteous-gf-carlito: Rod-thin strokes, big bowls. Righteous grabs attention with that cut-ribbon sameness, while Carlito, a sans-serif with open round letters and tight spacing, stays easy to follow once the text gets going.
gen-righteous-gf-changa: Changa has a lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals, tall and solid. Righteous leads with drafting-pen outlines of one nib width, and Changa does the steadier job of holding up paragraphs.
gen-righteous-gf-courier-prime: Righteous bends thin steel rod into big, round letters. Courier Prime sets a monospace line beneath, drafting-pen steady and structured, and the pair's real strength is how different their two voices stay.
gen-righteous-gf-days-one: Righteous cuts every stroke end from the same ribbon, bowls swelling to fill the line. Days One, a sans with rope-ladder spacing and a tall x-height, feels like a sturdy, friendly neighbor.
